title: Efficient Sampling for Many-Body Fermionic Non-Gaussianity
authors: Ryota Matsuda, Masahiro Hoshino, Yuto Ashida
abstract: Fermionic non-Gaussianity is a key resource for universal quantum computation, and its behavior in quantum many-body systems has attracted growing interest. Recently, a convolution-based measure, which we call the magic Rényi entropy (MRE), has been proposed as a resource measure of non-Gaussianity, but its evaluation is limited to small systems due to the computational cost growing exponentially with system size. In this work, we develop a perfect-sampling method to calculate the second-order MRE from matrix product states (MPSs). Our method uses a bounded estimator to control sampling fluctuations and a recursive sweep to draw the samples directly from the input MPS, which allows us to generate each sample with $\mathcal O(nD^3)$ time, where $n$ and $D$ denote the number of modes and MPS bond dimension, respectively. We benchmark our method on the XXZ chain with up to $128$ sites, demonstrating that the MRE captures intricate higher-order correlations at large scales, which are inaccessible to covariance-based measures. These results provide a computational tool that quantitatively evaluates many-body fermionic non-Gaussianity by accounting for higher-order correlations.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, efficient perfect-sampling algorithm to calculate the Magic Rényi Entropy ($	ext{M}_2	ext{RE}$), a resource measure quantifying fermionic non-Gaussianity. By operating directly on Matrix Product States, the method achieves polynomial scaling ($\mathcal{O}(nD^3)$) with system size. This allows researchers to quantitatively probe higher-order quantum correlations in fermionic systems like the XXZ chain, which are inaccessible to standard covariance-based measures.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing an efficient computational method to calculate the second-order Magic Rényi Entropy ($	ext{M}_2	ext{RE}$) for fermionic non-Gaussianity, as exact evaluation scales exponentially with system size.
main_result: The authors developed a perfect-sampling method that calculates $	ext{M}_2	ext{RE}$ in polynomial time ($\mathcal{O}(nD^3)$), successfully demonstrating that this measure captures higher-order correlations inaccessible to simpler covariance-based metrics.
method: The method employs a perfect-sampling technique using a bounded estimator and a recursive sweep to sample directly from Matrix Product States (MPSs), avoiding the explicit construction of replicated tensor networks.
model_or_system: The study focuses on many-body fermionic systems, benchmarked on the XXZ chain of spinful fermions, which are represented using a right-canonical MPS formalism.

important_parameters: System size ($L$), MPS bond dimension ($D$), and the anisotropy parameter ($\Delta$) of the XXZ chain.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the input state is represented by a right-canonical MPS and utilizes a bounded estimator to control sampling fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the MRE scaling for the XXZ chain, showing agreement with known analytical results for $\Delta=-1$ and saturation behavior for $\Delta<-1$. Other figures detail the structure of the sampling sweep using boundary matrices.
paper_structure: The paper develops the perfect-sampling technique for $	ext{M}_2	ext{RE}$ calculation, benchmarks it on the XXZ chain to confirm polynomial scaling and physical accuracy, and analyzes the saturation of the non-Gaussianity measure in different regimes.
why_interesting: The development of a polynomial-time sampling technique for higher-order correlation measures like $	ext{M}_2	ext{RE}$ is crucial for simulating complex quantum many-body physics that goes beyond simple quadratic Hamiltonians.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic illustration of the perfect-sampling sweep. The two parity-resolved boundary matrices encode the sampled prefix and are contracted with the local tensors of the input MPS and the beam splitter to obtain the conditional probabilities at each site. After the local output is sampled, the corresponding matrices are normalized and passed to the next site, yielding an exact Born sample without constructing the convolved MPS.

FIG. 2. (a) Second-order MRE of the ground state as a function of the number of sites L. At ∆= −1, the dashed black line is the large- L asymptotic form (18), and the circles are the perfect sampling from the exact MPS. The squares and triangles are the perfect sampling from the DMRG states at ∆= −1.02 and −1.005, connected by solid curves as guides, and the dotted horizontal lines are Eq. (19). The standard errors are smaller than 0.01 for all points. (b) shows the spin- spin correlation function Sz 1Sz j at ∆= −1.02 for L = 16, 32, 128 and ∆= −1.005 for L = 32, 64, 128.
